classes.name: Oral atypical antipsychotics
classes.description: Second-generation oral antipsychotics: aripiprazole, quetiapine IR/ER, olanzapine, risperidone, ziprasidone, lurasidone (Latuda), paliperidone ER, cariprazine (Vraylar), brexpiprazole (Rexulti), lumateperone (Caplyta), asenapine, iloperidone, clozapine, olanzapine/samidorphan (Lybalvi).
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or add-on treatment for depression.

classes.name: Long-acting injectable antipsychotics
classes.description: Long-acting injectables: aripiprazole (Abilify Maintena, Abilify Asimtufii, Aristada), paliperidone palmitate (Invega Sustenna/Trinza/Hafyera), risperidone (Risperdal Consta, Perseris, Uzedy, Rykindo), olanzapine pamoate (Zyprexa Relprevv), haloperidol and fluphenazine decanoate.
classes.plainDescription: A shot every few weeks or months instead of a daily pill.

records.verificationNote: Read PDL pp.44-46 (text layer; PA column). Oral SGAs listed with no PA: risperidone, quetiapine, aripiprazole, olanzapine, ziprasidone, lurasidone, paliperidone ER, clozapine. Auto PA on Caplyta, Fanapt, Lybalvi, Rexulti, Vraylar. Not listed on PDL (not coded nonformulary, list not stated complete): Saphris/asenapine, brand Latuda, Seroquel, Zyprexa, Symbyax. Judgment: risperidone 1 mg chosen as the lowest-cost common no-PA generic; aripiprazole is equally defensible. AHCA Auto PA doc has an oral antipsychotic polypharmacy edit (max 2 oral antipsychotics of different chemical entities per 60 days needs PA), noted here, not a per-drug PA.

preferredAgent.sig: Deep IM (gluteal) injection every 4 weeks. First dose: 10-15 times the daily oral dose if stabilized on 10 mg/day or less (10-20 times if higher or at risk of relapse); give no more than 100 mg in the first injection and the rest 3-7 days later (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: A shot into the muscle about once a month, given at the clinic.

records.verificationNote: Read PDL pp.31, 43-46. Haloperidol decanoate (100 mg/mL, age 18+) and fluphenazine decanoate are listed with no PA, so they are the preferred picks. Auto PA on the Abilify, Aristada, Invega, Erzofri, Risperdal Consta and Uzedy entries. Not on PDL: Perseris, Rykindo, Zyprexa Relprevv (not coded nonformulary; list not stated complete). Partial because the PDL does not say whether clinic-administered LAIs are paid under pharmacy or medical benefit; confirm with AHCA before relying on a pharmacy-benefit reading. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Haloperidol decanoate (no PA, age 18+) is named in the class definition and verified on PDL p.44; kept as the pick because it is the only LAI class member without an Auto PA edit. Judgment item: many prescribers would write Invega Sustenna or Abilify Maintena first, and those Auto PA edits pay at the counter when a schizophrenia or bipolar diagnosis is in claims. Fluphenazine decanoate also verified, no PA. Confirm the choice.]

records.verificationNote: Read PDF pp.69-72. Every LAI row carries Tier 6 and the SP (specialty) flag; none carries PA, ST or QL. Pick: the generic lowercase risperidone microspheres line (Tier 6, no PA), the lowest-barrier LAI on the list. The guide labels these self-administered specialty (SP) under the pharmacy benefit; clinic-given injections may route to the medical benefit, which this guide does not address. Sig is standard label dosing; the guide prints no sig. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: all LAIs (Risperdal Consta and generic risperidone microspheres, Perseris, Uzedy, Rykindo, Abilify Maintena/Asimtufii, Aristada, Invega Sustenna/Trinza/Hafyera, Erzofri, Zyprexa Relprevv, haloperidol/fluphenazine decanoate) confirmed Tier 6 + SP, no PA/ST/QL, PDF pp.69-72. Many are clinic-administered, so a medical-benefit route may also apply]

records.verificationNote: Tier and quantity-limit flags for the risperidone microspheres read by x-coordinate on page 38 (Tier 4, QL 2 per 28 days; no PA on any long-acting injectable on pages 35-38). Judgment: all long-acting options are Tier 4 with no PA, so the preferred pick is Risperdal Consta, a common product whose QL matches its every-2-week label dosing. Long-acting injectables are usually given in a clinic and may fall under the Part B medical benefit rather than Part D; the guide prints no BvsD flag on these rows, so the cost path is unconfirmed. Perseris, Uzedy and Rykindo do not appear in the guide. The guide does not state it is complete, so they are not recorded as excluded. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Re-confirmed against Humana formulary 26402, v17 (updated 10/01/2026), sources/humana-premier-rx-pdp-newtopics-2026-10.pdf (tier, PA, ST, QL read by x-coordinate; the v16 copy used in the first pass is superseded). Risperdal Consta is Tier 4, QL 2 per 28 days, no PA on page 38. Sustenna is on pages 36-37, Trinza on 37, Hafyera on 36. Stays partial: no BvsD flag is printed, so the Part B or Part D path for clinic-given injections is unconfirmed.]
